Chief_Complaint.source_text: CC: Difficulty breathing after insect sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient was stung on the arm a few minutes ago.
There is a local rash and puncture mark at the sting site.
Patient feels slight right lip swelling.
Patient reports breathing difficulty but not particularly acute.
Patient is anxious about possible worsening of symptoms.
Patient has never had an EpiPen.
No medications have been taken yet for this reaction.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of anxiety and panic attacks, not on medication.

Family_History.content: Patient denies relevant family illnesses or acute reactions.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient works as a computer scientist.

Assessment.content: Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp) with onset minutes ago and no current signs of anaphylaxis.
Assessment.source_text: 1) Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp) – no current signs of anaphylaxis; onset minutes ago

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommend chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg orally, 1 tablet up to every 4 hours, maximum approximately 6 tablets per day.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Antihistamine: Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg PO, 1 tab up to q4h (max ~6/day)

Plan_of_Care.content: Alternatively, use a once-daily non-sedating over-the-counter antihistamine from any chemist.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: OR once-daily non-sedating antihistamine (OTC, any chemist)

Plan_of_Care.content: Return to care or go to emergency department if lip or tongue swelling, shortness of breath, stridor, or worsening breathing occur.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Return/ED precautions: Lip/tongue swelling, SOB/stridor, worsening breathing

Plan_of_Care.content: If rapidly progressing symptoms occur, go straight to A&E.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: rapidly progressing symptoms go straight to A&E

Plan_of_Care.content: Monitor skin; if erythema spreads, the area becomes hot or tender, or there are signs of local infection, reassess as antibiotics may be needed.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Skin monitoring: If erythema spreads, area becomes hot/tender or signs of local infection → reassess; may need abx

Plan_of_Care.content: Education provided with information link on anaphylaxis and review of warning signs.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Education: Provided info link on anaphylaxis; warning signs reviewed

Plan_of_Care.content: No allergy testing now; consider allergy testing if recurrent reactions or rashes occur.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Testing: No allergy testing now; consider if recurrent reactions/rashes

Follow_up_Information.content: Follow-up as needed with a low threshold to contact if concerned.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: Follow-up: PRN; low threshold to contact if concerned

Physical_Findings.content: On video exam, breathing appears normal.
On video exam, lips are not swollen.
Oral and throat view on video exam is reassuring.
Arm shows slight erythema with puncture mark.
Physical_Findings.source_text: Arm: Slight erythema with puncture mark

Physical_Findings.content: Blotchy rash present on the arm at the sting site.
No visible swelling of the arm at the sting site.
